implementation_notes: Closures (impl Fn(&T) -> bool) are the raw carrier, but the combinator layer comes from the predicates crate: predicate::function(f) lifts any Fn(&T) -> bool, PredicateBooleanExt adds .and(), .or() and .not() returning composed AndPredicate/OrPredicate/NotPredicate values, and BoxPredicate type-erases a rule tree assembled at runtime - divide, choose and negation for predicates, with eval(&self, item: &T) taking the input by reference. Generic composition monomorphises; only the BoxPredicate boundary allocates.
pitfalls: eval takes &self and the item by reference: a rule that mutates shared state (a counter, a cache) makes the verdict depend on evaluation order - keep predicates pure.
BoxPredicate erases the type and allocates per node, so a rule set rebuilt per request pays for it; keep the typed AndPredicate/OrPredicate chain when the rule set is fixed.

variants.name: validator crate derive attributes (declarative, accumulating)
variants.implementation_notes: The validator crate puts rules on the data model: #[derive(Validate)] implements Validate and field attributes declare the checks (#[validate(email)], #[validate(url)], #[validate(length(min = 1))]) with custom(function = "...") for your own predicate. validate(&self) returns ValidationErrors, a map keyed by field path, so all field failures come back at once - the accumulating verdict an API or form needs. Composite structures are validated by deriving Validate at each level and calling validate() on the nested value from a custom function or the caller.
pitfalls: ValidationErrors is a map keyed by field path: flattening it into a single String at the boundary throws away the paths clients need to highlight a field.

Custom functions must have the exact signature fn(&T) -> Result<(), ValidationError>; a closure or an &str error does not compile, and the diagnostic points at the attribute rather than the signature.

variants.name: Zero-dependency closures plus enum dispatch
variants.idiom_name: Box<dyn Fn(&T) -> Result<(), E>> rule vectors + match on enums
variants.implementation_notes: With no dependencies the pattern is closures and enums: a rule is Box<dyn Fn(&T) -> Result<(), E>> (or impl Fn for monomorphised sets), a rule set is a Vec folded with accumulation or short-circuit, and choose is a match on an enum whose variants carry the branch data, which the compiler forces to be exhaustive. Reach for this in no_std crates, in zero-dependency libraries, and whenever a crate's fixed trait surface does not fit the rules you need; prefer impl Fn parameters over Box<dyn Fn> when the rule set is static, because they monomorphise to direct calls.
pitfalls: Box<dyn Fn> is neither Clone nor thread-safe by default: sharing a rule set across threads needs dyn Fn(&T) -> Result<(), E> + Send + Sync behind an Arc.
Returning heap-allocated error strings from every rule allocates on the happy path; in hot loops return Option<&'static str> or a small enum instead.
